security_audit.summary: Most static matches are lexical false positives caused by minified Motion code, JavaScript template literals, CSS, and documentation. Confirmed risks include third-party runtime resources, unescaped map marker HTML, permissive cross-window messaging, JavaScript evaluation during validation, and a mandatory GitHub update check. No prompt injection, credential access, covert command execution, or malicious intent was found. Static review was capped at 400/660 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 260 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Generated decks execute third-party JavaScript from CDNs, including a mutable Lucide latest URL.
remediation.suggestion: Vendor required libraries locally, pin exact versions, verify hashes, and apply a restrictive Content Security Policy.

remediation.issue: The Swiss map example inserts point names and metadata with innerHTML.
remediation.suggestion: Build marker elements with createElement and textContent, or sanitize every untrusted value before insertion.

remediation.issue: The presenter validator evaluates a JavaScript array expression extracted from the input deck.
remediation.suggestion: Parse speaker notes with a JavaScript AST or strict JSON parser, and reject expressions, calls, accessors, and other executable syntax.

remediation.issue: Presenter synchronization uses wildcard postMessage targets and does not validate event origin or source.
remediation.suggestion: Use a specific target origin, verify event.origin and event.source, and validate each message against a strict schema.

remediation.issue: The skill performs git fetch before obtaining consent for network access.
remediation.suggestion: Make update checks optional and request user confirmation before any network command.

remediation.issue: External fonts, stylesheets, and map tiles reveal network requests and reduce offline reliability.
remediation.suggestion: Self-host assets when possible and clearly disclose remaining network dependencies before generation.

content.value_statement: Building polished web presentations requires extensive layout and runtime work. This skill provides templates, design rules, presenter tools, and validation workflows.
actual_capabilities: Creates horizontal, single-file HTML slide decks from supplied topics, outlines, documents, or data.
Supports a magazine design system and a Swiss International Style design system.
Adds stable slide identifiers, speaker notes, timing plans, rehearsal records, and audience-screen controls.
Provides responsive layouts for statements, comparisons, timelines, images, metrics, and system diagrams.
Frames screenshots and plans generated visuals for predefined image slots and aspect ratios.
Validates presenter contracts and Swiss layouts with included Node.js scripts.
limitations: Produces HTML presentations, not editable PowerPoint or Keynote files.
Uses static files and does not provide collaborative editing or cloud storage.
Some fonts, icons, maps, and animation fallbacks require external network resources.
Visual quality still requires browser review across the intended display size.

use_cases.title: Prepare a product launch
use_cases.description: Turn product messaging, screenshots, and metrics into a Swiss-style launch deck with presenter notes.

use_cases.title: Build an editorial talk
use_cases.description: Convert an article or research narrative into a magazine-style presentation with a clear story arc.

use_cases.title: Deliver a technical briefing
use_cases.description: Present architecture, benchmarks, and workflows with structured diagrams, timing guidance, and audience synchronization.

prompt_templates.title: Create a short deck
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a seven-slide magazine-style HTML presentation about [topic] for [audience], using this outline: [outline].
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with a topic and short outline

prompt_templates.title: Transform source material
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn [document or article] into a ten-slide Swiss-style deck for [audience], emphasizing [key message] and [required data].
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request based on existing material

prompt_templates.title: Integrate visual evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a presentation from [outline], place screenshots from [folder] into suitable slots, preserve readable details, and add speaker notes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request with local visual assets

prompt_templates.title: Produce a rehearsable launch deck
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a [duration]-minute launch deck with stable slide IDs, timed notes, audience mode, generated visual plans, and complete validation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced production request with presenter requirements

output_examples.input: Create an eight-slide Swiss-style AI product launch for startup investors.
output_examples.output: A validated horizontal HTML deck with a bold cover, market evidence, product workflow, metrics, roadmap, closing page, and timed speaker notes.

output_examples.input: Turn this cultural essay into a magazine-style conference talk.
output_examples.output: A narrative HTML presentation with editorial typography, image-led layouts, section breaks, presenter notes, and keyboard, touch, and overview navigation.

output_examples.input: Build a technical briefing from architecture notes and dashboard screenshots.
output_examples.output: A structured web deck with screenshot framing, system diagrams, benchmark slides, stable page identifiers, presenter controls, and validation results.

best_practices: Provide the audience, duration, outline, required facts, and visual assets before generation.
Choose one design system and one approved theme for the entire presentation.
Review every slide in a browser and run the relevant validation scripts before presenting.
anti_patterns: Do not mix magazine and Swiss layout classes within one deck.
Do not invent facts, metrics, image content, or speaker actions that lack source support.
Do not compress overflowing content with unreadable text; split the slide or choose another layout.

faq.question: Does this skill create PowerPoint files?
faq.answer: No. It creates browser-based HTML presentations.

faq.question: Which design styles are available?
faq.answer: It supports an editorial magazine style and a Swiss International Style system.

faq.question: Can the presentation work offline?
faq.answer: Core HTML and local Motion assets can work offline. External fonts, icons, maps, or CDN fallbacks may not load.

faq.question: Does it include presenter notes?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports structured notes, slide purposes, timing, transitions, rehearsal records, and presenter controls.

faq.question: Can I use product screenshots?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide local files and required crop rules, sensitive-data handling, and target layout slots.

faq.question: How is the result checked?
faq.answer: Included validators inspect presenter contracts and Swiss layouts. Final browser review remains necessary.
